summary: Ran `npx -y -p @angular/cli@19 ng update @angular/core@19 @angular/cli@19 --allow-dirty --force` from EFNgApp/EFNgApp/ClientApp on Node 20/npm 10, bumping @angular/* to 19.2.25, the CLI/build-angular toolchain to 19.2.27, typescript to ~5.8.3, and zone.js to ~0.15.1. The mandatory @angular/core migration added `standalone: false` to all 7 NgModule-declared components (AppComponent, NavMenuComponent, HomeComponent, CounterComponent, FetchDataComponent, FetchEmployeeComponent, AddEmployeeComponent) since Angular 19 defaults new components to standalone; the optional 'use-application-builder' and 'provide-initializer' migrations were not applied, keeping the smallest correct change. The automated update left one build break that needed a manual fix: `BrowserModule.withServerTransition({ appId: 'ng-cli-universal' })` in app.module.ts no longer compiles because `withServerTransition` was removed from `BrowserModule` in Angular 19 (a TS2339/NG1010 error that, left unfixed, broke parsing of the whole NgModule.imports array and cascaded into unrelated-looking errors for every directive/pipe used across the app, e.g. routerLink, formGroup, ngClass). Fixed by importing `APP_ID` from `@angular/core`, replacing the call with plain `BrowserModule`, and adding `{ provide: APP_ID, useValue: 'ng-cli-universal' }` to AppModule's providers, which preserves the original app-id behaviour used for SSR transfer-state matching. Install and build both pass after this fix; test fails the same pre-existing way as baseline and every prior hop (angular.json's test target points at root-level styles.css instead of src/styles.css); `npm run build:ssr` (not a required check) still reports the same two pre-existing, unrelated TS typing errors (@types/jasmine, @types/ws), verified present before this hop's changes too.
changes: Upgraded typescript from ~5.4.5 to ~5.8.3 and zone.js from ~0.14.10 to ~0.15.1

@angular/core migration: added `standalone: false` to the @Component decorators of AppComponent, NavMenuComponent, HomeComponent, CounterComponent, FetchDataComponent, FetchEmployeeComponent and AddEmployeeComponent

Manual fix in src/app/app.module.ts: replaced removed `BrowserModule.withServerTransition({ appId: 'ng-cli-universal' })` with plain `BrowserModule` plus an `APP_ID` provider, since `withServerTransition` no longer exists on BrowserModule in Angular 19
package-lock.json regenerated by npm as part of the update/install cycles
manual_followups: npm install still needs legacy-peer-deps (set project-wide via ClientApp/.npmrc in an earlier hop) because @ngrx/* (^17.2.0) and @nguniversal/module-map-ngfactory-loader@7.1.0 declare peers on older @angular/* majors. @ngrx/* should move to its 19.x line and @nguniversal/module-map-ngfactory-loader should be replaced by @angular/ssr (the @nguniversal scope was merged into @angular/ssr from Angular 17 onward) in a later hop; the .npmrc override can likely be removed once both are resolved.

`npm run test` fails before any spec executes because angular.json's test architect target still points at `styles.css` at the ClientApp root instead of `src/styles.css`; this predates this hop (present since baseline) and was left as-is per the rule that pre-existing failures don't need fixing.

`npm run build:ssr` (not a required check) reports two pre-existing TypeScript errors from @types/jasmine and @types/ws type-definition conflicts; verified present before this hop's changes too, so left as-is.

Angular 19's optional 'use-application-builder' migration (webpack-based builder to the new esbuild/vite-based application builder) and 'provide-initializer' migration (APP_INITIALIZER -> provideAppInitializer) were not applied, to keep this hop's change minimal; worth revisiting in a later hop.

All NgModule-declared components now carry an explicit `standalone: false`; a later hop converting the app to standalone components (if desired) will need to remove these flags and restructure the module imports accordingly.
